title: Amber Friendship
text: “Or, well… Raphtalia-chan?”
“What?”
“To you, is the village a place? Or is it people?”
“Um…”
Big Sister lowered her head and began to think it over, indeed.
“I think… it’s the place where everyone is.”
“Right. That’s what I thought. That’s why we’re working hard to bring everyone back right now. As for the place, we can secure that wherever, eventually. Of course, here would be best.”
This was, I gathered, Father’s roundabout way of asking her to consider rebuilding the village somewhere else with its people, even if it wasn’t this exact spot.
“Yeah…”
But Big Sister’s expression suggested she hadn’t quite come to terms with it, even if she seemed to accept it on the surface.
“Let’s think about that part later, okay? Sadeena-san?”
At Father’s compromise proposal, Older Sister seemed to mull it over for a moment before nodding.
“Got it. Then Big Sister will help out too.”
“Yes, please just stay in safe Zeltoble with Raphtalia-chan and the others. I’ll guarantee your living expenses as much as I can.”
“Ohh? Even so, Big Sister can’t just live off your charity forever, you know?”
“I was hoping you could look after Raphtalia-chan and the others, if you would…”
Father made the suggestion tactfully, but Older Sister showed no sign of backing down.
“Of course, Big Sister will decide after seeing what she can actually help with. That’s fine, right?”
I supposed this was Older Sister’s own particular brand of cooperation.
“I suppose that’s fine, but…”
“You know, the heroes are putting on a circus to gather everyone. Everyone wanted to help, but they won’t let us.”

Big Sister’s friend explained to Older Sister. At that, Older Sister fixed her gaze on Father. Father, wearing a wry smile, seemed to be silently conveying to her—without a word—just what sort of “circus” this was. Being naturally perceptive, Older Sister apparently understood immediately from that alone.
“Got it. Big Sister will check things over properly first, then decide whether everyone can help. So wait a bit, okay?”
“Really? Make sure you ask properly!”
“Boo!”
And so, after making that promise with Big Sister and the others, Older Sister joined up with the group.

Once Older Sister joined the circus, Father’s operation grew even livelier. Incidentally, it was decided that Older Sister would be the one to check whether any of Big Sister’s fellow villagers were among those sold into slavery. Even from Father’s perspective, it apparently felt less burdensome to have Older Sister handle it rather than asking Big Sister directly. She really was reliable in all sorts of ways, I supposed.
“Ugh…”
“Aw, come on, Elmelo-chan~ You’ve still got plenty of room for more drinks~”
“I really do think Sadeena-san is drinking too much…”

After wrapping up the circus for the day, Father took the slaves, Elephant, and Older Sister out to a demi-human tavern in town as a reward for everyone’s hard work—only for Older Sister to promptly drink Elephant under the table, indeed. The drinking money, incidentally, came from a separate stash—funds earned from selling off Three Heroes Church attackers. Since Father was the only one who could really keep up with Older Sister, I ended up standing by a bit further off. The Siltvelt envoy and the monster dealer’s subordinates were left minding the fort, since it was a place they were already familiar with, and Father, ever considerate, figured they’d rather not get dragged into Older Sister’s drinking bout.
“Wolf-chan, don’t you want a drink too~?”
“Vow-vow!”
Wolf let out a warning growl in response to Older Sister’s invitation.
“Now now, drink up~”
“Vauf—”
Glug, glug, glug… Older Sister poured drink after drink into Wolf. The first sip was met with wariness, but by the second, Wolf was drinking of its own accord.
“Kuh… kuun. Hic… kukuun.”

Eventually, Wolf began letting out little sobbing whimpers directed at Older Sister, tears streaming down, before latching onto Father instead. From there Wolf kept babbling on in kuun-kuun noises about something or other, though I hadn’t the faintest idea what.
“Is Wolf one of those crying drunks?”
“Kuun… kukuun. Vow!”
Then Wolf wrapped some cloth around its head like a bandana and, with a forceful rrrip, tore it clean apart.
“Fuu… fuu…”
And finally, still worked up, Wolf collapsed face-first onto the table.
“Hmm… that’s a strange way to get drunk, Wolf.”
“Ohh~?”

With that, Older Sister’s gaze fell upon her next targets—the half-breed lizardman and the rabbit man. The rabbit man flinched instantly and scrambled to put the half-breed lizardman between himself and her like a shield.
“How about you, Shion-chan? Drink up and enjoy yourself~”
“I’m enjoying myself in my own way. I don’t much care for getting blackout drunk, and I intend to keep my position in mind.”
“Is that so~?”

“…I do hope the village can be rebuilt. You have my support. So please, don’t get everyone drunk just to dig out their true feelings. Theodore and I both wish to be of use to Shield Hero’s cause. Surely that’s true of you as well?”
“Big Sister only just joined, so she wants to get along with everyone~”
“Spare me that… Since we’re on the subject, I’d like you to train me.”
“Ohh~?” Older Sister let out a startled sound at the half-breed lizardman’s words.
“Even though Elmelo-chan is the combat advisor?”
“You’re quite the formidable fighter yourself, aren’t you. Teach me how you fight… I’m still far from skilled enough. Wolf has technique too, but your movements look far sharper.”
Then the half-breed lizardman glanced my way for a moment. What was that about? Did he want me to teach him too? Perhaps noticing that glance, Father turned to look at me as well.
“Should we have Motoyasu-kun join in on Shion’s training too?”
“I know that one’s the strongest, but I don’t want to learn from just one person—I want breadth, from many teachers.”
“I see. So then, Sadeena-san, what do you think?”
“Eh, Big Sister isn’t all that strong, so she’s not sure she can really teach anything~”
I could sort of tell Older Sister was being cautious. Once she trusted someone, she tended to open up and engage rather easily.

“…Before the first wave came, I heard a rumor. That in a certain village in Seaetto territory, there was someone frighteningly strong at both drinking and fighting. Sadeena—that would be you, wouldn’t it?”
“Guess Big Sister was quite the celebrity~”
“Not that much, really~ Big Sister wasn’t even there when it mattered most.”
Older Sister set her glass down on the table, seemingly caught up in some regret, and traced the rim with her finger.
“Big Sister was out on a long-range fishing trip, at the request of the Seaetto lord. The sea got real rough out there too… and Big Sister was the only one who made it back.”
“Sadeena-san…”
Father seemed to sympathize with Older Sister.
“When the ship was sinking, everyone’s fathers begged Big Sister—if you survive, please look after our children.”
Apparently Older Sister had been out on the open sea when the first wave struck. Others helping with the fishing had been aboard too, and the ship had sunk—that was the story she’d told afterward.
“…It wasn’t at the lord’s request. That was… an order from the crown.”
“Oh, was it now.”

The half-breed lizardman added this, sounding somewhat displeased. Now that I thought of it, I recalled hearing something like that before—something about the Crimson Swine returning after a long absence and demanding some rare fish from distant waters. That woman truly was a plague upon everyone, I say.
“I won’t tolerate ill words about Seaetto. If nothing else, he stood at the front, guiding his people to safety to minimize the damage from the waves.”
“And then he goes and dies, leaving everyone else to deal with the mess? Everyone was in real trouble because of it~”
Thud! The half-breed lizardman slammed his fist onto the table, clearly displeased.
“Shion?”
Snapping back to himself with a start, the half-breed lizardman looked at Father.
“…Forgive me. What she says is fair. Still, I’d like it understood that he truly was a lord who cared for his people—that much was true.”
“Big Sister isn’t denying that either, you know. He was a real loss… truly, he was.”
On that point, at least, they seemed to share the same understanding.
